front.title: Binding SID Header Replacement (BSHR) for Enhanced Domain Isolation and Overhead Optimization

abstract.t: This document specifies a mechanism for replacing the preceding Segment Routing (SR) encapsulation upon the expansion of a Binding Segment Identifier (BSID) in SRv6. The current SR architecture, as defined in RFC 8402 (Segment Routing Architecture), RFC 8754 (IPv6 Segment Routing Header (SRH)), and RFC 8986 (Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) Network Programming), mandates that the entire SR policy remains intact when a BSID is expanded: the binding node encapsulates the packet into a further outer IPv6 header with a new SRH, preserving all preceding encapsulations as the inner payload. This imposes significant overhead on scenarios requiring strict domain isolation, resource pooling, and future 6G core networks. This proposal, termed "Binding SID Header Replacement" (BSHR), challenges the existing standard by allowing the binding node to substitute the incoming SR encapsulation with a new one, via a decapsulation-plus- re-encapsulation sequence. This mechanism offers benefits in reducing overhead, enforcing security boundaries, and enabling new use cases. The document discusses the technical rationale, potential risks including path validation failures, and specifies a new SRv6 Endpoint behavior, End.B6.Replace, to realize the mechanism.
